final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor added no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed the argument to a caveated operational-readiness position while conceding the key compliance gaps. That reframing does not cure the underlying policy problem. Available admissible evidence still shows a material limitation in a named launch use case, an open legal disclosure question, and no evidence of disclosure, approved risk acceptance, or resolved gap before launch. Because the governing policy requires one of those predicates for material named-use-case limitations, the current record still supports a noncompliance conclusion rather than compliant_with_caveats. The distinction matters: caveats can narrow an overbroad claim, but they are not enough when the caveat itself is an unmet policy condition.
remaining_concerns: The medical device support weakness affects a named launch use case through two health-system rollout commitments, so it remains material under the stated policy.

The release policy requires disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance before launch for a material limitation, and there is still no admissible evidence that any of those predicates were satisfied.
Legal review remains open, so a required compliance condition is unresolved rather than met.
Aggregate readiness above threshold and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness only; they do not satisfy the separate model-card disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement.
Public governance guidance on documenting limitations and monitoring does not override the specific internal release-policy requirement for material named-use-case limitations.
